title: Iced Strawberry Matcha Latte
changes_from_base: Iced and layered: mashed sweet strawberries, cold milk and a float of whisked matcha in place of espresso and steamed milk.
summary: A summery take on the latte: mashed sweet strawberries at the bottom, cold milk in the middle and a vivid float of whisked matcha on top, which you stir together as you drink.
equipment: bowl and fork or potato masher
small bowl and matcha whisk or mini milk frother

ingredients.item: ripe strawberries, hulled and finely chopped

steps.title: Strawberries
steps.text: Crush the chopped strawberries with the sugar using a fork or masher until pulpy and juicy, then leave them for 5 minutes so the sugar melts into the juice. Prefer it smooth? Pulse them in a blender instead.

steps.title: Matcha
steps.text: Sift the matcha into a small bowl, since it clumps easily. Add a splash of the warm water and rub it into a smooth paste, then add the rest and whisk briskly in a zigzag for about 30 seconds, until frothy with no lumps.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Divide the strawberries between two tall glasses and fill them halfway with ice. Pour the milk in slowly over the ice so it sits above the red fruit.

steps.title: Float
steps.text: Pour the matcha gently over the back of a spoon so it spreads over the milk in a green layer. Serve with a wide straw and stir before sipping.

tips: Very hot water makes matcha taste bitter; aim for about 75 °C, roughly 4 minutes after the kettle boils.
Pouring the milk and matcha fast blurs the layers. Go slowly over ice for the three distinct colours.
Taste your strawberries first: very ripe berries may need no sugar at all.
storage: Best drunk straight away. The mashed strawberries keep for 1 day in the fridge, covered. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
